title: Migration orchestrator: immutable backup headers, linear trace annotations, and rollback dry-run shim
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Private upgrades suffer from restore mismatches, interrupted applies, and schema regressions that surface only after roll-forward. This PR adds a small, opt-in orchestration layer (migration-orchestrator) to reduce human error and make rollbacks observable. It combines three core mitigations: immutable backup manifest headers stored with snapshots, Linear ticket annotations on every migration step for traceability, and a rollback dry-run shim that simulates revert paths (terraform plan + Helm dry-run with preflight hooks) to detect blockers before executing a real rollback.

What changed: Introduces a CLI binary (installer/bin/migrator) and operator controller hooks that sequence: backup verification, schema compatibility checks, staged terraform apply, canary quiesce, and optionally a rollback simulation. Key features: (1) Immutable manifest headers (backup-id, source-cluster, schema-version, sha256) are written alongside snapshot objects in S3/GCS and validated prior to restore to avoid cross-cluster restores. (2) Linear-trace: each migration step embeds a Linear key in logs and migration records so audits and support can correlate run artifacts to the originating ticket. (3) Rollback dry-run shim: new command runs terraform plan against the target rollback state using the last-known manifest and executes Helm dry-run with our migration hooks to reveal ordering, schema, and hook failures that would otherwise be discovered only while mutating live state. The shim also enforces a downgrade guard: automated downgrades are blocked when schema_compat reports regressions unless explicitly acknowledged with a flag.

Compatibility and safety: Migrator is gated by an operator feature flag; default installer behavior is unchanged. Backups created by older installers remain visible but restore will be blocked if the manifest header is absent unless the operator passes --force-legacy with an explicit reason. The rollback guard defaults to on for private deployments to prioritize safety.

Testing: Added e2e tests under test/e2e/migrator that run a staged migration and a simulated rollback using localkind clusters and mocked storage providers. CI added an integration matrix that runs: bootstrap, backup/verify, terraform-plan (rollback shim), and helm-dryrun stages.

Operational: New telemetry metrics introduced: migrator_run_total, migrator_failures_by_stage, backup_manifest_mismatch_count. Documentation: docs/upgrade-playbook.md updated with an enablement checklist, runbook steps, and examples for staged restores and rollback rehearsals.

Related linear tickets: ENG-4721 (migration auditability), ENG-4875 (rollback dry-run automation).

review_thread: Diego Alvarez: Nice work — I like the manifest headers. A few questions: how do we rotate manifests for long retention buckets?
Maya Thompson: We add a generation timestamp and rely on lifecycle rules; migrator ignores manifests older than max_generation_age to avoid accidental restores from stale snapshots.
Priya Kapoor: Schema validator looks solid. Can the downgrade guard be default-on? We should err on the side of safety for private installs.
Maya Thompson: Agreed. Switched the guard to default-on and added a --allow-downgrade advanced flag. Tests updated.
Samir Choudhury: CI flagged a hook naming collision with existing Helm hooks; please rename to quiesce-migrator-prehook.
Maya Thompson: Renamed the hook, pushed fix, and reran CI. Lint and helm tests now pass.
Diego Alvarez: Approve after green CI.
ci_checks: lint: initially fail -> fix pushed -> pass
release_notes:
- Adds migration-orchestrator CLI to sequence backup verification, schema checks, staged applies, and rollback dry-run.
- Writes immutable backup manifest headers (backup-id, sha256, schema-version) with snapshots to reduce restore mistakes.
- Adds rollback dry-run shim using terraform plan + helm dry-run to surface rollback blockers.
- Adds Linear trace annotations for auditability and new migrator telemetry metrics.
additional_context: This change is intentionally conservative: migrator is opt-in and does not change existing restore semantics unless enabled. Operators should rehearse rollback-dry-run in staging with representative snapshots before enabling in production. Enterprise customers get an enablement checklist in the docs.
